statement_record.intree: Class Monad := { ret {x} : x ~> M x; join {x} : M (M x) ~> M x; fmap_ret ... ; join_fmap_join {x} : join ∘ fmap (@join x) ≈ join ∘ join; join_fmap_ret {x} : join ∘ fmap (@ret x) ≈ id; join_ret {x} : join ∘ @ret (M x) ≈ id; join_fmap_fmap ... }
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — [M : C ⟶ C] is the endofunctor T, [ret]/[join] are eta/mu, [join_fmap_join] is Riehl's associativity square and [join_fmap_ret]/[join_ret] are his two unit triangles, all stated with the hom-setoid ≈ in place of =. statement_record.book: The monad axioms are exactly the monoid axioms; a monad on C is precisely a monoid in the monoidal category C^C of endofunctors, with composition as the binary functor and id_C as the unit object. evidence.intree_statement: Context (R : Reflective S). Definition Reflective_Monad : @Monad C (Incl C S ◯ reflector R) := Adjunction_Induced_Monad (reflective_adj R). Definition Reflective_IdempotentMonad : @IdempotentMonad C (Incl C S ◯ reflector R) Reflective_Monad.
Definition join_iso_iff_ret_M_iso (x : C) : IsIsomorphism (@join C M _ x) ↔ IsIsomorphism (@ret C M _ (M x)) := (join_iso_ret_iso x, ret_iso_join_iso x).
Definition join_iso_fmap_ret (x : C) (Hj : IsIsomorphism (@join C M _ x)) : fmap[M] (@ret C M _ x) ≈ @ret C M _ (M x).

statement_record.book: Prove the equivalence of three characterizations of an idempotent monad (T, eta, mu): (i) mu is a natural isomorphism; (ii) mu is a monomorphism; (iii) eta T = T eta as natural transformations T => T^2. Then show, as a fourth separate clause, that the adjunction of a reflective subcategory of C induces an idempotent monad on C.
statement_record.intree: Class IdempotentMonad {C} (M : C ⟶ C) `{@Monad C M} := { idem_join_iso {x} : IsIsomorphism (@join C M _ x) }; join_iso_iff_ret_M_iso (x : C) : IsIsomorphism (join x) ↔ IsIsomorphism (ret (M x)); join_iso_fmap_ret (x : C) (Hj : IsIsomorphism (join x)) : fmap[M] ret ≈ ret (M x); Reflective_IdempotentMonad : @IdempotentMonad C (Incl C S ◯ reflector R) Reflective_Monad.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the equivalence, same on the trailing clause. The trailing clause (reflective subcategory => idempotent monad) is fully proved as Reflective_IdempotentMonad, over Reflective_Monad = Adjunction_Induced_Monad of the reflection adjunction, and the library goes further than the exercise by proving the converse and the Eilenberg-Moore equivalence (Idempotent_Reflective, Idempotent_EM_Equivalence). But characterization (i) is taken as the DEFINITION in tree (IdempotentMonad's single field is pointwise invertibility of join), so no equivalence with (ii) or (iii) is established: only the forward implication (i) => (iii) is proved (join_iso_fmap_ret), and the one genuine two-way result, join_iso_iff_ret_M_iso, characterizes (i) by invertibility of ret at M x — a condition Riehl does not list.

gap: The three-way equivalence is not proved. Missing entirely: (ii) 'mu is a monomorphism' — the word Monic never appears in Construction/Reflective/Idempotent.v and no lemma anywhere states that a monic join is invertible (grep for 'Monic (@join', 'join.*Monic' over *.v returns 0 hits), so neither (i) => (ii) (trivial) nor the substantive (ii) => (i) exists. Missing: the converse (iii) => (i), i.e. that eta T = T eta forces mu to be invertible — only join_iso_fmap_ret, the direction (i) => (iii), is proved. Missing: any packaging of the three conditions as a single equivalence statement. Also, the in-tree conditions are stated pointwise as IsIsomorphism at each object rather than as invertibility of the natural transformation mu; that is equivalent in this setting and not counted as part of the gap.
